 $$s =~ s/### Plates and objects pane \(deferred\)
.*?(?=### Agent WebView)/### Plates and Project pane

The pane is a fork-owned native surface (`Shell/LeftPane`) that sits left of the workspace on Prepare. It lists every plate, including a one-plate project, and a second tab holds the saved project's identity, the model's 3MF metadata, the physical-print history, version history, and export. It adds no project state and no undo path: it paints what two GUI-free models describe and sends each click to a workspace command.

| Piece | Owns |
|---|---|
| `Workspace/ProjectOutline.hpp`, `IWorkspace::outline()` | The read model: plates, copies (with the plate that holds each), volumes, customization and mesh facts, and the selection below the object level. Plate membership comes from `PartPlateList`; nothing is inferred from where a copy sits. |
| `Shell/LeftPaneModel` | What rows the Plates tab shows and when: the active plate is open, others are folded with a summary computed from the current copies, children exist only for data that exists, "Not on a plate" appears only for a copy no plate holds. Also the tab and Project-subview navigation. |
| `Shell/ProjectPaneModel` | The Details and Print history views as data. A field nobody recorded is absent; a slicer estimate is kept apart from the measured duration; a ledger record with nothing to show is counted, not drawn. |
| `Workspace/OrcaOutline.cpp` | The adapter's side: `select_plate`, `add_plate`, `select_copy`, `select_volume`, `plate_actions`, `run_plate_action`. Each ends in the path Orca's own UI takes (`Plater::select_plate_by_hover_id`, the toolbar's Add plate event, `Selection` plus the canvas's object-select event), raised synchronously on the GUI thread so a command returns with its effect in place. |
| `Shell/LeftPane`, `LeftPaneProject.cpp` | Painting and input. Painting records where each control landed and the pointer reads that record, so a click can only hit what was drawn. |

The physical-print ledger has any number of subscribers (`ProjectPersistence::subscribe_ledger`), so the pane and the header's overflow menu observe it independently.

/s; });

Plate rows are 32 DIP, object rows 36 DIP, both on `surface.canvas` blocks with the standard radius and a 2 DIP gap; a folded plate adds a 20 DIP Metadata summary line indented 32 DIP. ### A canvas event posted from a command had not run when the command returned

`GLCanvas3D::post_event` queues the event with `wxPostEvent`. A workspace command
that used it to add a plate, or to tell Orca a selection changed, returned with
the plate count and the object list unchanged, and the following read saw the
old state. Commands that must have taken effect when they return raise the event
on the canvas window with `ProcessEvent` (`raise_now` in `Workspace/OrcaOutline.cpp`).

### `Plater::select_object` returns early when the canvas already holds the selection

It skips `ObjectList::update_selections()`, so the object list can still be
pointing at the plate it last showed. The object list's own commands
(`toggle_printable_state`, `set_extruder_for_selected_items`, `fix_through_cgal`)
act on the list's selection and do nothing, without an error, when it is not an
object or a copy. Bring the list up to date first, and check the effect: a
command that can silently do nothing needs its result read back.

### The object list changes the model without announcing it

Switching an object's printable state or filament through the list publishes no
project-state change, so a view built on the workspace stays as it was. The
command that calls the list publishes a Contents change itself.

### Orca gives every loaded object the first filament slot

An object's config carries `extruder = 1` from the start. It is an assignment,
not a choice, so presence of the key says nothing about whether the person chose
it; the pane shows a filament only for a multi-material job or a slot other than
the first.

### A plate carries settings only by Orca's own test

`PartPlate::config()` has keys on every plate. The plate icon's "has plate
settings" test is bed type, print sequence, first-layer and other-layers
sequences, or a spiral-mode setting; the pane uses the same one.

input.content:
# Plates / Project pane: handback

Working notes for Kenneth, 2026-10-03. Untracked on purpose; the code is on `claude/open-figma-browser-86ed07` (commits `2742276f5f`, `01610d3162`, and the one after them). Built from the handoff `left-pane-implementation-handoff.md`, starting fresh as asked (the other worktree's uncommitted pane was not used).

## What exists

| Area | Where |
| --- | --- |
| Read model: plates, copies (each with the plate that holds it), volumes, customization and mesh facts, exact selection below the object | `Workspace/Workspace.hpp` (`ProjectOutline` and friends), `Workspace/ProjectOutline.hpp` (pure questions: folded summaries, off-plate copies, children) |
| Adapter side | `Workspace/OrcaOutline.cpp`: `outline`, `select_plate`, `add_plate`, `select_copy`, `select_volume`, `plate_actions`/`run_plate_action`, `object_actions`/`run_object_action`, `toggle_copy_printable`, `open_customization` |
| Pane rows and navigation, no GUI | `Shell/LeftPaneModel` |
| Project views as data (metadata, print history) | `Shell/ProjectPaneModel` |
| The pane | `Shell/LeftPane.cpp` (Plates tab, tabs, menus, input), `Shell/LeftPaneProject.cpp` (Project tab) |
| Tokens | `component.leftPane` in `design-tokens.json`, parsed in `ShellTheme`, guarded in `test_brand_tokens.cpp` and `test_shell_theme.cpp` |
| Ledger with any number of subscribers | `ProjectPersistence::subscribe_ledger` (replaces the single `set_ledger_listener`) |
| Moved out of the header's overflow menu | Version history, Export project 3MF…, Project details, the print count. Recent projects, Back to Prepare, Preferences, Switch to classic view stay |

Every pane command ends in the path OrcaSlicer's own UI takes: `Plater::select_plate_by_hover_id` for plate clicks and the plate icons' actions, the toolbar's Add plate event, `Selection` plus the canvas's object-select event for copies and parts, the object list for printable/filament/repair, `Plater::set_number_of_copies`/`split_object`, `delete_items` for copies and parts, gizmo managers for the customization tools. The pane keeps no project state and no undo path.

## Verification (private tree `C:\b\opf`, Release, Windows Server 2022, software GL, 200% display scaling)

| Suite | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `workspace_contract_tests` | 275 assertions pass (new: outline, selection, plate/object actions) |
| `jusprin_tests` | 502 assertions pass (new: pane model, Project model) |
| `shell_theme_tests`, `agent_bridge_tests` | 132 and 5222 assertions pass (agent: three new ledger-subscriber cases) |
| `brand_tokens_tests` | passes; the one `[!mayfail]` case fails as before |
| `workspace_adapter_integration_harness` (real Plater) | 835 pass, 0 fail; 42 are new `pane_` checks |
| `shell_integration_harness --left-pane` | light and dark pass: plate click reaches Orca, canvas selection comes back, tab switches keep plate and selection, Escape at the Project root is not taken, add plate with undo/redo, both menus, lock/unlock, printable switch, the customization mark, metadata and Details, a recorded print and Print history, Version history with restore, edit info |
| `--external-project-history`, `--classic-switch`, `--stock` | pass (history test ported to the pane) |
| `shell_integration_harness` default mode | see the last line of this file; the four pre-existing failures are `failed_autosave_is_visible`, `failed_autosave_has_plain_status_text`, `failed_autosave_blocks_project_release`, `earlier_model_version_available` (the test makes a directory read-only with POSIX permissions, which Windows ignores) |

One inherited test bug fixed: `verify_reopened_local_versions` kept `HEAD` and `current-state.json` open while the store replaced them, which Windows refuses (three `close()` calls).

Not verified: 100% and 150% scaling (the RDP session has to be reconnected at those scales), macOS, Linux, screen readers, `npm test` in AgentUI/HomeUI (no change to either, but not run).

## Fork stewardship evidence

One OrcaSlicer-owned file changed: `src/slic3r/GUI/Project.hpp`, 3 lines. `ProjectPanel::show_info_editor(bool)` moves from the private section to the public one, so **Edit Project Info** opens OrcaSlicer's own editor through its own method. Nothing upstream was deleted or rewritten; one declaration moved a few lines.

- Rebase simulation: `git merge-file` with base `38ac3e9e1a`, ours `HEAD`, theirs `upstream/main` `6a07853933` (2026-09-26), whose `Project.hpp` has since changed `m_sequence_id` on the line above: merges with no conflict and the result is correct (upstream's atomic line kept, declaration public). `git merge-tree` over the whole fork cannot run: this fork and upstream share no merge base.
- Fork now owns: product policy only, plus one neutral seam (a declaration made public). No upstream behavior was copied.

Fork-owned files touched outside the pane: `HeaderControls` (an exported `draw_header_icon`, and `HeaderMenu::open` takes an alignment so a menu from the left column opens rightward), `ShellController` (the column, visibility, project sources, Agent pane's maximum width leaves the canvas its minimum), `StatusRow` (project entries removed), `ProjectPersistence`.

## Decisions to confirm

1. **Prepare only.** The pane shows on Prepare, not Preview or Home. Version history, export, details and the print count are therefore reachable only from Prepare now.
2. **Tabs land at their top level.** The Project tab always opens at its root; the Plates tab leaves a Project subview. A new project keeps the tab but drops any subview and all expansion.
3. **Object extruder.** Orca gives every loaded object slot 1. A filament is shown only for a multi-material job or a slot other than the first.
4. **Mesh problems.** "Mesh error" (danger) for remaining open edges, "Mesh repaired" (warning) for auto-repaired ones; the customization mark is a separate gray diamond.
5. **Cost.** A print record's stored cost is never shown: the record has no currency.
6. **Move to front** is offered below the first plate; **Filament grouping** on dual-extruder Bambu printers; **Delete** while another plate remains (Orca's own conditions or their sensible reading, since stock shows Move to front always).
7. Focus ring only for keyboard navigation.

## Gaps against the handoff

- **Figma copy and some structure could not be read directly.** The built-in browser pane is too narrow to read the file visually, and its right-click menus are unreliable. What was read: exact CSS for 26c2 (all geometry in `component.leftPane` comes from it) and the layer structure of every frame from the layers panel. Wording the layer names do not carry is my own: the object menu's first three rows (Figma has "Menu/Row" instances whose text I could not read), the folded-summary phrasing, status words, section labels. Please compare the captures in this folder with the frames, or export the frames and I will correct them.
- **Not in the pane:** per-object settings (no tool exists in the shell to open them; the mark lists the count, disabled), the 26h comparison board itself, "Split to parts", accessible names for painted rows (hit regions carry labels; no `wxAccessible`), resize or collapse (deliberately absent).
- **Attachments:** category rows open their files with the system program; the cover shows up to one (root) or three (Details) "Model Pictures".
- **Dark values** come from existing tokens; `status.successSubtle` for a "Sliced" chip does not exist because the frames I read show the status as plain secondary text.

## Incident to know about

While trying to read Figma, a menu keystroke on frame **26d2 · Object row menu** started Figma's "Rename layers" (AI) for a moment. I canceled it and pressed Ctrl+Z; the layer names read back afterwards match what they were before ("Chat Header", "Pinned Setup Card", "+ Add plate"), but please glance at 26d2's version history in Figma to be sure nothing was renamed.

## Captures

`*-light.png` and `*-dark.png` in this folder are the pane itself drawn by the harness (the popup menus are separate windows and are not in them).

content.text:
The Plates / Project pane is built and committed on `claude/open-figma-browser-86ed07` (three commits, `2742276f5f` to `f12bff98a1`). It matches the handoff's behavior, but I couldn't read all of the Figma wording, so some labels are my own guesses. It sits left of the canvas on Prepare only.

- **Plates tab:** every plate is listed, and the active one opens. Folded plates show a summary computed from their current copies. Rows show copies, filament, mesh and customization marks, and a "Not on a plate" group.
- **Project tab:** project name and save state, model metadata with a cover picture, Details, print history from the ledger, version history with restore, export, and Edit Project Info (opens Orca's own editor).
- **Menus:** plate, object, copy and part overflow menus all run Orca's own commands. The handoff's collapse and resize (frame 26g) are not built.

I started fresh as you chose. The other worktree's uncommitted pane was not used.

## What I ran

- **Unit and contract suites:** workspace contract, pane model, brand, theme and agent suites all pass.
- **Real-Plater harness:** 835 checks pass, 42 of them new.
- **Shell scenarios:** the new `--left-pane` scenario passes in light and dark. History, classic-switch and stock still pass.
- **Default shell scenario:** 508 pass and 4 fail. Those four were failing before my changes (they rely on POSIX read-only directories).

I fixed one inherited Windows test bug: a harness step left files open that the store then tried to replace.

I did not check 100% or 150% scaling (the session is at 200%), macOS, Linux, screen readers, or `npm test` in AgentUI and HomeUI.

## Things to know

1. **Figma incident.** While reading Figma, a keystroke on frame **26d2** started its "Rename layers" AI. I canceled it and pressed Ctrl+Z, and the layer names read back unchanged. Please glance at 26d2's version history to be sure.
2. **Figma copy.** The browser pane was too narrow to read the frames visually. I got exact CSS for 26c2 and the layer names of the other frames. Menu row labels, summary phrasing and status words are my best guess. Compare the captures in the handback folder with the frames. Or export the frames and I'll fix them.
3. **Header menu change.** Version history, export, details and the print count moved out of the header's overflow menu into the Project tab. They're now reachable only on Prepare, since the pane doesn't show in Preview or Home.
4. **One Orca file touched.** `Project.hpp` has one declaration made public, 3 lines, so Edit Project Info can open Orca's editor. It merges cleanly onto current upstream.
5. **Missing item.** Per-object settings have no entry in the object menu because the shell has no tool to open them. The customization mark lists the count, disabled.

## Decisions for you

- **Prepare only.** Is hiding the pane in Preview OK, given item 3?
- **Tab landing.** Each tab always opens at its top level, and a new project drops any open Project subview. The handoff was ambiguous. Is that the behavior you want?
- **Cost.** A print record's cost is never shown, because it stores no currency. Do you want it shown anyway?

content.text:
Both changes are in, committed as `3e27740c2e`.

- **Per-object settings:** I removed the "N object settings changed" row from the customization mark's menu. An object customized only through per-object settings still gets the gray mark, but the mark does nothing when clicked. It opens a menu only when a painting or layer-height tool made the customization. The object overflow menu never had a per-object settings entry.
- **Cost:** Print history now shows the slicer estimate's cost as `$` plus two decimals, for example `Slicer estimate: 2 h 5 min · 42 g · $3.20`. It is hidden when the stored cost is zero.

The unit tests and the pane scenario in light and dark pass. I did not rerun the full default scenario for this small change.

Here are the two questions I asked, said more plainly.

**Prepare only.**
- The new left pane appears when you're on Prepare. It's hidden on Preview and Home.
- Version history, export, details and the print count used to be in the top-right "…" menu on every screen. I moved them into the pane's Project tab, so now you can only reach them from Prepare.
- If you want them on Preview too, I'd show the pane there as well. I haven't decided to; you said you don't follow the question, so I left it as is.

**Tab landing.**
- Clicking the Project tab always shows the Project front page, even if you were last looking at Details or Print history.
- When you open or create a different project, the pane drops any open Project subview and forgets which objects you had expanded.
- The handoff didn't say what should happen here, so I picked these. If that's fine, there's nothing for you to do.

It's hidden on Preview and Home - we don't have Preview screen. make sure you didn't completely mess it up as this is usually a sign of some big mixup.
the project and plate tabs state (active/inactive, expanded/collased) don't need to be persisted. Did you write the code to persist them?
